# Implementation Guide — feat-39e1-recovery

**Generated by**: `/task-review TASK-REV-F30A` → `[I]mplement`
**Origin review**: [TASK-REV-F30A](../../backlog/TASK-REV-F30A-analyse-feat-39e1-autobuild-run-3-failure.md)
**Origin report**: [.claude/reviews/TASK-REV-F30A-review-report.md](../../../.claude/reviews/TASK-REV-F30A-review-report.md)
**Date**: 2026-05-10

## Goal

Unblock the FEAT-39E1 GB10 demo. Recovery from FEAT-39E1 autobuild run-3 failure (PH1-004 max_turns_exceeded due to a stale-worktree `.gitignore` silently dropping Player-authored files in `src/study_tutor/adapters/`).

## Wave Plan

The six follow-up tasks split into a sequential critical path (study-tutor, demo-blocking) and an independent parallel cluster (guardkit, defence-in-depth).

### Critical path — study-tutor repo (sequential)

```
Wave 1 → Wave 2 → Wave 3
```

| Wave | Task                                                                                       | Mode   | Complexity | Effort     | Dependencies                  |
|------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|------------|------------|-------------------------------|
| 1    | [TASK-NATS-FIX-004](TASK-NATS-FIX-004-manual-implement-command-router.md) — hand-implement PH1-004 from prior-run evidence | manual | 4          | ~1 hour    | none                          |
| 2    | [TASK-NATS-FIX-005](TASK-NATS-FIX-005-recreate-feat-39e1-worktree.md) — delete + recreate FEAT-39E1 worktree | direct | 1          | ~5 minutes | TASK-NATS-FIX-004              |
| 3    | [TASK-NATS-FIX-006](TASK-NATS-FIX-006-resume-autobuild-from-wave-5.md) — resume autobuild from Wave 5 | manual | 2          | ~3-6 hours unattended | TASK-NATS-FIX-005              |

**Why sequential**: Wave 1 must land `command_router.py` + tests on `main` and flip PH1-004 to `completed` in the feature.yaml before Wave 2 (otherwise the recreated worktree won't have the file). Wave 2 must remove the polluted worktree before Wave 3 (otherwise the autobuild runs again on the broken `.gitignore`).

**Total wall-clock to demo-readiness**: ~half a day focused (1h coding + 5min ops + 3-6h unattended autobuild watch).

### Defence-in-depth — guardkit repo (parallel-eligible, independent)

These three tasks can run in any order, in parallel, against the upstream `guardkit` repo. None block the critical path. None block each other.

| Task                                                                                                              | Mode      | Complexity | Effort     | File location                                                |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| [TASK-FIX-IGNR](../../../../guardkit/tasks/backlog/TASK-FIX-IGNR-classify-gitignored-vs-fabricated-in-coach-claim-audit.md) — classify gitignored-vs-fabricated in claim audit | task-work | 5          | ~0.5 day   | `~/Projects/appmilla_github/guardkit/tasks/backlog/`         |
| [TASK-FIX-RBSS](../../../../guardkit/tasks/backlog/TASK-FIX-RBSS-rollback-should-reset-sdk-session-and-preserve-audit-trail.md) — rollback resets SDK session + preserves audit trail | task-work | 6          | ~0.5 day   | `~/Projects/appmilla_github/guardkit/tasks/backlog/`         |
| [TASK-FIX-HEAB](../../../../guardkit/tasks/backlog/TASK-FIX-HEAB-honesty-rolling-average-early-abort.md) — honesty early-abort on sustained low rolling average | task-work | 3          | ~1-2 hours | `~/Projects/appmilla_github/guardkit/tasks/backlog/`         |

**Why defence-in-depth**: each addresses a *symptom* of the root cause that would have made run-3 fail less catastrophically (warning instead of max_turns; clean rollback recovery; early abort with diagnostic). After all three ship, a future stale-worktree-gitignore situation surfaces as a single warning on turn 1 with the `git check-ignore` rule named in the message — instead of a 5-turn 12-minute SDK burn followed by a forensic post-mortem.

## Execution Strategy

### Recommended ordering

1. **Day 1 morning**: TASK-NATS-FIX-004 (1h) → TASK-NATS-FIX-005 (5min) → kick off TASK-NATS-FIX-006 (autobuild starts running unattended).
2. **Day 1 afternoon (parallel with TASK-NATS-FIX-006 running)**: pick up TASK-FIX-HEAB (1-2h) in the guardkit repo. Smallest of the upstream tasks; quickest cycle for re-engaging the autobuild work.
3. **Day 1 end**: TASK-NATS-FIX-006 completes; verify with `/feature-complete FEAT-39E1`.
4. **Day 2-3**: TASK-FIX-IGNR (0.5d) and TASK-FIX-RBSS (0.5d) at leisure — these are upstream improvements with no demo deadline.

### Parallel execution (Conductor)

Since the three guardkit tasks are independent and live in a different repo, running them in Conductor workspaces is straightforward:

```
guardkit-repo-fix-ignr    (TASK-FIX-IGNR)
guardkit-repo-fix-rbss    (TASK-FIX-RBSS)
guardkit-repo-fix-heab    (TASK-FIX-HEAB)
```

The three study-tutor tasks should NOT use Conductor — they are sequential and the manual-mode tasks (FIX-004, FIX-006) are operator-driven, not delegated.

## Failure Modes To Watch

If any wave deviates from the expected behaviour, the most likely surfaces:

| Wave | Symptom                                                                                                       | Likely cause                                       | Action                                                                                                          |
|------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1    | `pytest tests/unit/adapters/test_command_router.py` fails after authoring                                     | nats_core API drift since 2026-05-08 spec          | Compare against current `~/Projects/appmilla_github/nats-core/` API; adjust imports/calls; ACs unchanged        |
| 2    | `git worktree remove` errors with "contains modified or untracked files"                                       | Something in worktree was edited after rollback     | `git -C .guardkit/worktrees/FEAT-39E1 status` first; commit or stash if needed; `--force` only when clean        |
| 3    | Wave 5+ Player hits "Checkpoint claim audit failed" message                                                    | Another `.gitignore` rule dropping a different path | `git check-ignore -v <path>` from log; add a re-include to the project root `.gitignore`; commit; resume         |
| 3    | Dependency-resolver crash on `deferred` PH1-010 predecessor                                                    | guardkit version predates TASK-FIX-DEFD             | Update guardkit; or re-do the soft-deps fix from TASK-REV-D509 in `FEAT-39E1.yaml`                              |
